metaTitle: Land Possession Recovery Suit Bangladesh 2026 | Section 8 & 9 Specific Relief Act
metaDescription: Legal guide on reclaiming dispossessed land in Bangladesh under Section 8 and 9 of the Specific Relief Act 1877, Section 145 CrPC, and Land Crime Prevention Act 2023.
keywords: specific relief act section 8 and 9 bd
heroIntro: When real property is unlawfully grabbed or encroached upon, the dispossessed owner can seek civil remedies under Sections 8 & 9 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 along with penal action under the Land Crime Prevention and Redress Act 2023. Authored by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court Advocate. Chamber contact: 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: ⚡ Core Legal Remedies for Land Grab
points: Section 9 Suit (Summary Possession): Must be filed within 6 months of dispossession without proving ownership title.
Section 8 Suit (Title & Possession): Filed within 12 years based on title deeds, khatians, and ad-valorem court fees.
Section 145 CrPC: Prevents breach of peace and secures status quo before Executive Magistrate.

sections.heading: 1. Section 8 vs Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act 1877
sections.content: Section 9 protects bare possession against unlawful eviction irrespective of title, while Section 8 determines substantive proprietary rights and ownership.

sections.heading: 2. Strict 6-Month Limitation under Section 9
sections.content: Any person dispossessed without consent otherwise than in due course of law must institute suit within 6 months. No appeal lies against a decree under Section 9.

sections.heading: 3. Declaration of Title and Recovery under Section 8 & 42
sections.content: Under Article 142 and 144 of the Limitation Act 1908, a comprehensive title suit can be instituted within 12 years subject to ad-valorem court fees.

sections.heading: 4. Criminal Penalties under Land Crime Prevention Act 2023
sections.content: Encroachers and illegal grabbers face rigorous imprisonment up to 7 years and substantial monetary fines under the latest 2023 enactments.

sections.heading: 5. Executing Decrees with Court Nazir and Police Force
sections.content: For enforcement of possession decrees through civil execution proceedings, consult Supreme Court Advocate Md. Shah Alam at 01712655546.

faq.question: What is the court fee for Section 9 suit?
faq.answer: Half the regular ad-valorem court fee of a standard title suit.
